XMLDB.COMMENT: mooDesk schema. Every table and field carries its own COMMENT; how the tables relate, and why, is DEVELOPER.md section Database schema. XML comments are not used here: the XMLDB editor drops them on save, COMMENT attributes survive.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_department
TABLE.COMMENT: Help desk departments, which act as queues: the unassigned tickets in a department are visible to every agent who is a member of it. Phase 3+.

FIELD.NAME: isactive
FIELD.COMMENT: 1=active, 0=archived (soft delete).

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_dept_member
TABLE.COMMENT: Agent-to-department membership, one row per pair. Drives both the assignment dropdown for a ticket and which tickets an agent sees in the Department view. Phase 3+.

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: Agent user ID. Must hold :agent capability to be assignable.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_category
TABLE.COMMENT: Ticket categories. parentid supports hierarchy and is populated, though the UI renders a flat list. Archiving is soft (visible=0) so foreign keys stay intact. The General seed row is created by db/install.php, not by this schema. Phase 3 adds departmentid.

FIELD.NAME: parentid
FIELD.COMMENT: Nullable. Sub-category parent reference. Null for root categories.

FIELD.NAME: departmentid
FIELD.COMMENT: Phase 3: optional link to a department. Null = applies to all departments.

FIELD.NAME: visible
FIELD.COMMENT: 0=archived (soft delete, preserves FK integrity), 1=active.

FIELD.NAME: usermodified
FIELD.COMMENT: 0 for system-seeded records.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_ticket
TABLE.COMMENT: Help desk tickets. The central entity. Status transitions are enforced by the service layer state machine, not by the schema.

FIELD.NAME: courseid
FIELD.COMMENT: Null for site-level tickets. Set for course-scoped tickets.

FIELD.NAME: contextid
FIELD.COMMENT: Moodle context ID snapshot. Write-once at creation. Not used for capability checks in Phase 1.

FIELD.NAME: coursename_snapshot
FIELD.COMMENT: Course fullname at creation time. Survives course deletion.

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: The requester: whose problem is this. Immutable after creation.

FIELD.NAME: createdby
FIELD.COMMENT: Who created the record. May differ from userid when an agent creates on behalf of a user.

FIELD.NAME: assigneeid
FIELD.COMMENT: Currently assigned agent. Null if unassigned.

FIELD.NAME: categoryid
FIELD.COMMENT: Nullable at DB level. Service layer always sets a value (default category fallback).

FIELD.NAME: departmentid
FIELD.COMMENT: Phase 3: department/queue this ticket belongs to. Null = globally visible to all agents.

FIELD.NAME: status
FIELD.COMMENT: 0=new, 1=open, 2=pending, 3=on_hold, 4=resolved, 5=closed. Transitions enforced by service layer state machine.

FIELD.NAME: priority
FIELD.COMMENT: 0=low, 1=normal, 2=high, 3=urgent.

FIELD.NAME: source
FIELD.COMMENT: 0=web (Phase 1 only), 1=email (Phase 2), 2=api (Phase 2).

FIELD.NAME: timefirstresponse
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp of first agent public reply. Null until first response.

FIELD.NAME: timeresolved
FIELD.COMMENT: Timestamp when status transitioned to resolved.

FIELD.NAME: timeclosed
FIELD.COMMENT: Timestamp when status transitioned to closed.

FIELD.NAME: sla_breached
FIELD.COMMENT: Phase 2 SLA enforcement flag. Always 0 in Phase 1-3.

FIELD.NAME: sla_paused_seconds
FIELD.COMMENT: Total seconds this ticket has spent in status=pending across all closed pause intervals. Added to the resolution deadline by sla_service. Never includes the interval currently open — see sla_paused_since.

FIELD.NAME: sla_paused_since
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp when the currently open pause started, i.e. when the ticket entered status=pending. NULL means the ticket is not paused right now. Closing a pause folds the elapsed time into sla_paused_seconds and sets this back to NULL.

FIELD.NAME: usermodified
FIELD.COMMENT: Last user to modify this record.

INDEX.NAME: ix_departmentid_status
INDEX.COMMENT: Supports VIEW_DEPARTMENT agent workspace queries at volume.

INDEX.NAME: ix_timemodified
INDEX.COMMENT: Supports the dashboard's recent-activity panel, which orders the whole table by last touch and takes the top few rows.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_reply
TABLE.COMMENT: Ticket thread: public replies, internal notes, and system event entries. Attachments hang off a reply through the reply_attachment file area keyed by reply id, including the opening message of a ticket, which is stored as the first reply.

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: Author. For type=system_event this is the actor who triggered the event.

FIELD.NAME: messageformat
FIELD.COMMENT: Moodle FORMAT_* constant. 1=FORMAT_HTML.

FIELD.NAME: type
FIELD.COMMENT: 0=public_reply, 1=internal_note, 2=system_event.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_ticket_history
TABLE.COMMENT: Immutable audit log of all ticket state changes. Insert-only.

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: Actor who caused the change. 0 for system-initiated actions.

FIELD.NAME: action
FIELD.COMMENT: String constant from ticket_history domain class.

FIELD.NAME: oldvalue
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON-encoded previous value. Null for creation events.

FIELD.NAME: newvalue
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON-encoded new value. Null for deletion events.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_incident
TABLE.COMMENT: Operational incidents: one row per CLASS of absorbed failure, not per occurrence. Identified by fingerprint (unique), counted by occurrences, and bounded in time by timefirstseen/timelastseen. Whether an incident is a CURRENT problem is derived from timelastseen against the configured active window, never stored; status records only what an administrator decided. Written by incident_service, which never throws. Operational observability (OBS-01).

FIELD.NAME: fingerprint
FIELD.COMMENT: sha1(source|code|scopekey). Unique: at most one row per class of failure, so a reappearance updates rather than inserts.

FIELD.NAME: source
FIELD.COMMENT: Closed set: observer, webhook, email_ingestion, scheduled_task.

FIELD.NAME: code
FIELD.COMMENT: Stable source.operation.condition identifier, e.g. observer.ticket_created.notify_failed. Never derived from an exception message.

FIELD.NAME: severity
FIELD.COMMENT: warning, error or critical.

FIELD.NAME: message
FIELD.COMMENT: Short human-readable summary, truncated and passed through the secret redactor before it lands here.

FIELD.NAME: context
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON object restricted to the allowlist in the incident domain class. Never holds credentials, email content or ticket content.

FIELD.NAME: occurrences
FIELD.COMMENT: How many times this class of failure has been recorded since timefirstseen.

FIELD.NAME: status
FIELD.COMMENT: Administrative intent: open, acknowledged (silences alerts) or resolved. Not a statement about whether the failure is still happening.

FIELD.NAME: timefirstseen
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp of the first occurrence in this row's lifetime.

FIELD.NAME: timelastseen
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp of the most recent occurrence. Drives the derived health state.

FIELD.NAME: timelastalerted
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp of the last alert sent for this incident; NULL when never alerted. Written by the alerting unit (OBS-03); the column ships here so the table takes one migration, not two.

FIELD.NAME: severityalerted
FIELD.COMMENT: Severity this incident was last alerted at; NULL when never alerted. An escalation past this value alerts again immediately, which is how a critical bypasses the cooldown without alerting on every cron tick.

FIELD.NAME: acknowledgedby
FIELD.COMMENT: userid of the administrator who acknowledged it; 0 once anonymised by a privacy erasure request.

FIELD.NAME: timeacknowledged
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp of the acknowledgement.

FIELD.NAME: resolvedby
FIELD.COMMENT: userid of the administrator who resolved it; 0 once anonymised by a privacy erasure request.

FIELD.NAME: timeresolved
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp of the resolution.

TABLE.NAME: local_moodesk_kb_article
TABLE.COMMENT: Knowledge base articles. One row per article in one language; rows sharing a groupid are translations of each other, one per language (KB-06). Body is stored as typed and cleaned on render, never on write.

FIELD.NAME: groupid
FIELD.COMMENT: Identity shared by every language variant of one article. Equals the row's own id for the canonical (source-language) row; the repository sets it on insert, so no persisted row keeps the default 0. When the canonical row is deleted the service re-points the survivors to the lowest surviving id.

FIELD.NAME: lang
FIELD.COMMENT: Moodle language code of this variant (en, es, pt_br). Unique within a group.

FIELD.NAME: categoryid
FIELD.COMMENT: Optional local_moodesk_category the article is filed under. Shares the ticket taxonomy by product decision (2026-09-12); treated as an opaque reference by the KB code.

FIELD.NAME: body
FIELD.COMMENT: Article HTML exactly as authored (PARAM_RAW). Rendered through format_text() without noclean or trusttext; see db/access.php.

FIELD.NAME: bodyformat
FIELD.COMMENT: Moodle FORMAT_* constant for body. FORMAT_HTML.

FIELD.NAME: searchtext
FIELD.COMMENT: Derived from body on every write: tags stripped, entities decoded, whitespace collapsed, lower-cased. What search matches against, so markup never does.

FIELD.NAME: status
FIELD.COMMENT: 0 draft, 1 published, 2 archived. Constants on the kb_article domain class.

FIELD.NAME: audience
FIELD.COMMENT: 0 everyone who may view the knowledge base, 1 agents only. An access rule, decided by kb_access_policy.

FIELD.NAME: createdby
FIELD.COMMENT: userid of the author; 0 once anonymised by a privacy erasure request.

FIELD.NAME: usermodified
FIELD.COMMENT: userid of the last editor; 0 once anonymised by a privacy erasure request.

FIELD.NAME: timepublished
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp of the first publication; NULL while never published. Not reset by unpublishing.

INDEX.NAME: ux_groupid_lang
INDEX.COMMENT: One translation per language per group (KB-06). Also serves every lookup by groupid, so no separate groupid index.
